value.body: A three-year postgraduate degree in Siddha medicine, taken after BSMS. Students specialise in one subject — such as Pothu Maruthuvam (general medicine), Noi Naadal (pathology and diagnosis), Gunapadam (pharmacology), Nanju Maruthuvam (toxicology), Kuzhandhai Maruthuvam (paediatrics) or Varma Maruthuvam — and complete a dissertation.

items.label: Entrance exam
items.note: Conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA)

items.label: Regulator
items.note: National Commission for Indian System of Medicine

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BSMS degree with internship completed and registration as a Siddha practitioner. Admission is through AIAPGET; all-India quota seats are allotted through Ayush central counselling and state-quota seats through state counselling (mainly Tamil Nadu).

value.title: At a glance
items: Siddha PG seats are few and concentrated in Tamil Nadu — for example the National Institute of Siddha, Chennai, and the Government Siddha Medical College, Tirunelveli (Palayamkottai).
Each subject has only a handful of seats, so options narrow sharply by rank.
An MD opens teaching posts in Siddha colleges, research posts (such as at CCRS) and specialist practice.

value.note: Counts for the Siddha paper only; MD (Siddha) seats are far fewer than candidates. The 2025 figure is from news reports of the NTA release.
